notes.text: Make the mayonnaise in two batches of 2 yolks each; one bowl of yolks can't take more than about 1 cup of oil by hand without strain.

move.title: The mayonnaise is the dish
move.body: Ensaladilla rusa is on the counter of nearly every tapas bar in Spain: potatoes, carrots, peas, and tuna, bound in mayonnaise and served cold. What makes it is the mayonnaise, made by hand from pasteurized yolks cooked to 160°F and built drop by drop into an emulsion.

why.title: One size, one pot
why.body: Potatoes cut to 1 cm and carrots to 6 mm finish together in the same water: the denser carrot is cut smaller. The peas only need the last minute.

why.title: Cold water start
why.body: Potatoes started in cold, salted water heat through evenly, so the outside doesn't fall apart before the center is tender. The salt seasons them all the way through.

why.title: Steam them dry
why.body: Spread on a sheet pan, hot vegetables give off their surface water as steam. Dry vegetables hold the mayonnaise; wet ones thin it and make the salad weep.

why.title: Yolks to 160°F
why.body: Pasteurized eggs are heat-treated in the shell, and the USDA says they can be used raw. This app cooks every egg to 160°F. Yolks whisked with lemon juice over gentle steam thicken at that point, and once cooled they emulsify oil just as raw yolks do.

why.title: Drop by drop, then a stream
why.body: Lecithin in the yolk coats each oil droplet and keeps it apart from the others. At the start there are too few droplets to stabilize a flood of oil, so the first quarter goes in a drop at a time. Once it's thick, a thin stream is fine.

why.title: Cool before binding
why.body: Warm vegetables would loosen and split the mayonnaise. Cooled to room temperature, then bound, then chilled, the salad holds its shape and stays out of the danger zone.

wrong.sign: The mayonnaise broke into oily curds
wrong.fix: In a clean bowl, whisk 1 teaspoon of mustard with 1 teaspoon of water, then whisk the broken mayonnaise into it a teaspoon at a time.

wrong.sign: The yolks scrambled over the water
wrong.fix: The water was boiling or you stopped whisking. Start again with new yolks over barely simmering water, whisking constantly.
They cooked too long. Check them a minute before the timer; a knife should slide in with no push.
The vegetables went in wet or warm. Next time steam them dry and cool them fully first.

quiz.q: Why is the carrot diced smaller than the potato?
choices: It's denser and cooks more slowly

quiz.q: Why does the first oil go in a drop at a time?
choices: There aren't yet enough droplets to stabilize a lot of oil
quiz.explain: Once thick, a thin stream is fine.

quiz.q: What temperature do the yolks reach?
quiz.explain: The app cooks every egg to 160°F.

quiz.q: Why cool the vegetables before adding the mayonnaise?
choices: Warm vegetables loosen and split it

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and carrots. Cut the potatoes into 1-cm dice and the carrots into 6-mm dice.
Put the potatoes and carrots in the pot with the vegetables' salt and cold water to cover by 3 cm. Bring to a boil, then simmer.
Add the peas and cook until a knife slides into a potato cube with no push.
Drain, then spread the vegetables on the sheet pan to steam dry and cool to room temperature.
Bring 3 cm of water to a bare simmer in the saucepan for the yolks.
Separate the eggs, dropping the yolks into the heatproof bowl. Keep the whites for another use.
Wash your hands and wipe the counter.
Whisk the lemon juice and the mayonnaise's water into the yolks. Set the bowl over the water and whisk constantly until it thickens and holds a trail.
Probe the yolks: 160°F. Take the bowl off the heat, set it on a damp towel, and whisk for a minute to cool it.
Whisk in the mustard and the mayonnaise's salt. Combine the oils, then whisk them in drop by drop for the first quarter, then in a thin stream.
steps.look: Thick, glossy, and pale, holding a ribbon on the surface.

steps.text: Taste and adjust with lemon and salt. It should be sharper than you'd eat on its own; the potatoes will soften it.
Flake the tuna into the large bowl. Add the cooled vegetables and two thirds of the mayonnaise, and fold with the spatula until coated.
Mound the salad on the plate and smooth the remaining mayonnaise over the top. Cut the peppers into strips and lay them on with the olives.
Cover and refrigerate until cold. Keep it chilled and serve within 2 hours of taking it out; it keeps 3 days in the fridge.
steps.tip: In Spain it's served cold with breadsticks or bread.
